title: Writing may have started as a way to count

probes.question: What kind of job may writing have first grown out of?
options: Recording amounts of livestock and goods

probes.question: True or false: clay tokens were gradually replaced by flat tablets marked with a stylus.

image.alt: A late Uruk clay tablet with pressed round numerals and early pictographic signs recording goods, displayed in a museum case
image.credit: Osama Shukir Muhammed Amin FRCP(Glasg) / Wikimedia Commons

panels.text: Before writing, people kept track of goods with small clay tokens. Each token is thought to have stood for a specific amount of livestock or other commodities.
The tokens were pressed into the surface of round clay envelopes, called bullae, and then stored inside them.
Little by little, flat clay tablets replaced the tokens. Signs were recorded on them with a stylus.
Writing is first recorded in Uruk, at the end of the 4th millennium BC. Cuneiform is thought to stem from a token system used for accounting, though how the tokens were used is still debated.
